text: Write a program showing that floating-point addition is not associative. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: double left  = ___;                 // group the first two
double right = ___;                 // group the last two
explanation: Verified: 0.6000000000000001, then 0.6, then false. Addition of real numbers is associative; addition of doubles is not, because each intermediate result is rounded to the nearest representable value and the two groupings round differently. This is not a curiosity — it is why a parallel sum can disagree with a sequential one, since splitting the work changes the grouping, and why reproducible numerical results require fixing the order of operations.
